svg.title: What USPS pages say about addressing an envelope: return address, delivery address placement, line by line format, letters and formatting tips, and packages.
svg.text: How to address an envelope
What the USPS pages say
Return address
Top left corner, in the same format as the
delivery address. The FAQ says to always use
one; the video calls it a requirement.
Delivery address
In the center (FAQ, video) or bottom center
(letters page). The popup says to write it
parallel to the longest side.
Line by line
Name or company, street address, then city,
state and ZIP+4. Apartment or suite: on the
street line (FAQ, video) or its own line above
the street (letters page).
Letters and formatting
FAQ and letters page: capital letters, no
commas or periods. The video: write legibly,
avoid red or smearing ink, print labels if
you can, and writing words out is encouraged.
Packages
Address, return address and postage on the
same side, address parallel to the longest
side. A printed label can replace a separate
address label; do not bend, fold or overlap.
Sources: USPS FAQ, USPS.com pages and a USPS
video transcript; none shows an update date;
read Nov. 13, 2026
